children: rose 7.04% premarket after reporting first-quarter revenue of $19.3 billion, up 30%, and non-GAAP earnings of $1.92 per share, up 30%. Cloud infrastructure revenue grew 121% to $7.4 billion. Remaining performance obligations reached $664 billion, up $209 billion year over year, after Oracle booked more than $30 billion of new AI cloud contracts and delivered 850MW of additional data center capacity. It also delivered more than 300,000 GPUs to AI cloud customers since the end of the fourth quarter, almost triple the capacity delivered in the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026. Software revenue fell 3% to $5.5 billion as customers moved off premises.

Operating cash flow hit $23.1 billion, up 184%, but $11.36 billion of that came from customer prepayments carrying a significant financing component, which Oracle deducts in its own net cash outlay table. Capital expenditure was $28.5 billion against $8.5 billion a year earlier, leaving free cash flow at negative $5.4 billion. Oracle also sold $20 billion of common stock through an at-the-market program during the quarter, but management said that the new contracts won't require incremental capital.
Oracle now guides to at least $90 billion of full-year revenue and $8.10 of non-GAAP EPS, with second-quarter revenue growth of 30% to 34%.

title: Oracle's RPO Reaches $664 Billion With Cloud Infrastructure Up 121%
